learning: Mass 0.5 at y = 0.08 tests whether a lighter robot holds the s-bend and slalom gain while lifting oval progress. If s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.15 or the oval oscillation rises sharply with no progress gain, the lighter robot is over-responding, and mass 0.6 should be restored.
notes: Iteration 8 robot: the Builder's mass 0.5 kg test on the iteration 7 design. Controller unchanged, so the race isolates mass.
rationale: The Builder's iteration 8 proposal changes one thing from iteration 7: mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Geometry is otherwise identical: 16 mm sensors at y = 0.08, x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.16 by 0.14 m. The controller is unchanged from iterations 3 to 7 (kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, sensor_weights 25 times x, last_direction), so there is no gain compensation to add. Iteration 7 (y = 0.08, mass 0.6) is the best design so far at 75.92. Its oval progress was 0.2725 but oval steering_oscillation was 0.18, and its slalom had 1.0 line losses per run. Iteration 6 (mass 0.6, y = 0.07) and iteration 3 (mass 0.8, y = 0.07) showed that lowering mass from 0.8 to 0.6 cut s-bend oscillation (0.144 to 0.140) and lifted oval progress slightly. Mass 0.5 lowers yaw inertia further, so the robot turns more readily at the same kp. I expect the oval to hold its gain, and the main risk is extra oval and s-bend oscillation. I also keep the Builder's decision rule in mind: if s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.15 the next step is to restore 0.6. Mass 0.5 is within the 0.4 to 1.5 kg limit, and the design is a single-variable test against iteration 7.
